title: success-paths-and-access-blueprint-2024
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview
--------
This playbook defines the operating model for role enablement, first‑year tooling access, and career stage expectations at Redwood. It harmonizes People Ops workflows, the internal toolchain, and engineering/product role ladders so new hires and movers get the right access, learning path, and milestones with minimal friction.

Purpose
-------
- Reduce friction and time-to-impact for new hires and internal role changes.
- Centralize ownership and SLAs for access requests and provisioning.
- Provide a transparent, stage-based career enablement blueprint that aligns onboarding tasks with measurable milestones.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all full-time employees, contractors with >3 months engagement, and interns on multi-month rotations. Covers: provisioning for company systems (SSO apps, cloud accounts, repositories, internal dashboards), mandatory training, role-specific tool access, and first-year staged milestones.

Principles
----------
1) Least Privilege by Default: roles receive minimal default access; additional access is granted via documented approval flows.
2) Time-to-Impact Targets: new hires should reach baseline productivity within 30 days and role-level competence within 120 days.
3) Self-Serve When Safe: automated badges and access requests are preferred for low-risk tools; manual approvals retained for sensitive systems (KMS, billing, production clusters).
4) Stage-aligned Learning: onboarding tasks map to defined career stages and measurable outputs.

Role & Career Stage Matrix (summary)
----------------------------------
Columns: Role Family | Typical Entry Level | 30d Baseline | 120d Competency | Access Tier
| Engineering | SWE-I | Local dev environment, repo read + CI debug | Can ship small bugfixes, own a low-risk service | Tier 2 (dev infra, staging)
| Product | PM-I | Product wiki, analytics dashboards | Run small scope features end-to-end | Tier 1 (product analytics)
| Infra/SRE | SRE-I | Monitoring dashboards, dev clusters | Triage incidents, own runbooks | Tier 3 (prod oncall with approvals)
Notes: Tier 1 = non-sensitive business tooling; Tier 2 = staging infra and feature flags; Tier 3 = production infrastructure, KMS, billing.

Onboarding & Access Checklist (first 30 days)
-------------------------------------------
1. Pre-Start (People Ops): create SSO account, set up device stipend and hardware order, assign buddy and manager. Target: 5 days before start.
2. Day 0–3: account activation, MFA enrollment, company policies acknowledgement, baseline security training (30 min).
3. Day 3–10: toolchain setup: local dev environment, repo access, CI read, Slack & calendar groups. Badge provisioning: Developer-Basic / Product-Basic / Analyst-Basic.
4. Day 10–30: sandbox tasks, first PR or product write-up, mentor check-ins weekly, request additional scoped access (databases, staging) via Access Request form.

Access Request Flow (owners and SLAs)
-----------------------------------
- Low-risk (Tier 1)
  - Owner: People Ops 
  - Process: Self-serve portal (Internal Access Hub) -> auto-approval if role mapping matches.
  - SLA: 8 business hours for provisioning.
- Medium-risk (Tier 2)
  - Owner: Team Lead (Engineering/Product) + Infra approver
  - Process: Submit request in Access Hub -> Slack notification to approvers -> manual approval -> provisioning job.
  - SLA: 2 business days.
- High-risk (Tier 3)
  - Owner: Security + Product/Infra Manager
  - Process: Access Hub -> security review -> logged justification + training completion -> ephemeral credential issuance where possible.
  - SLA: 3–5 business days depending on context.

Example: request production DB read access (Tier 3)
1. Submit Access Hub form with justification, linked ticket or runbook entry.
2. Attach manager approval (email or Slack thread).
3. Security reviews logs, requests brief architecture note from requestor.
4. If approved: ephemeral read-only credentials issued for 12 hours; long-term access requires quarterly re-approval.

Request CLI snippet (for self-serve tooling)
------------------------------------------
# Authenticate via SSO and request a staging cluster role
redwood-iam login --sso
redwood-iam request-access --resource staging-cluster --role dev
# Returns: request_id and estimated SLA

Training & Role Ramp Curriculum
------------------------------
- Mandatory (all hires): Security Essentials (30m), Code of Conduct (15m), Data Handling Primer (20m).
- Role-specific 30d tracks: Engineering Setup & CI, Product Metrics 101, Analytics SQL primers.
- 120d stretch goals: own a small project, present a demo at team retro, pass a role-specific checklist review with manager.

Access Matrix (condensed table)
------------------------------
Service | Default for New Hire | Request Flow | Tier
staff-ldap | No | People Ops auto-provision | 1
repo-org | Read | Manager request for write | 2
staging-cluster | No | Team Lead approval -> infra provisioning | 2
prod-cluster | No | Security + Manager approval -> ephemeral creds | 3
billing-console | No | Finance approval required | 3
KMS/HSM | No | Security-only with audit justification | 3

Stage-based Milestones and Signals
----------------------------------
- Day 30 Signal: first merged PR or product spec, buddy sign-off on environment.
- Day 60 Signal: independent troubleshooting of a minor incident / ability to run central integration tests.
- Day 120 Signal: owns an end-to-end card, delivered and reviewed; manager checklist completed.

Escalation & Exceptional Cases
-----------------------------
- If a provisioning SLA is missed by >48 hours, the People Ops on-call (escalation channel #people-ops-escalations) is notified and a ticket is auto-created with urgency P2.
- For denied high-risk requests, Security will provide a written rationale and recommend mitigations (read-only, ephemeral, masked dataset).

Maintenance & Ownership
-----------------------
- People Ops: maintain baseline badges, onboarding timeline, and low-risk provisioning.
- Engineering Enablement: owns developer templates, CI keys, and local dev guides.
- Security: governs Tier 3 approvals, quarterly access reviews, and audit evidence.
- Team Leads: validate role competency milestones and sign access approvals for Tier 2 items.

Operational Metrics (tracked in Redwood Console)
---------------------------------------------
- Mean time to provision (by tier) — target: Tier1 < 8h, Tier2 < 48h, Tier3 < 72h.
- % of new hires reaching Day 30 signal — target: 90%.
- Quarterly access review completion rate — target: 100% for Tier3 scoped owners.

Frequently Asked Questions
-------------------------
Q: I need temporary production access to investigate a customer issue.
A: Open an urgent Access Hub request and tag your manager and security in the form. For high-severity incidents, on-call security provides emergency elevation (audited, ephemeral).

Q: How do I change roles internally and keep my progress?
A: Submit a Role Change form via People Ops; your new manager coordinates a tailored 30/120-day ramp that recognizes prior accomplishments. Access re-evaluated by role mapping.
